deities: Sri Varaha Swamy (Adi Varaha, the boar avatar of Vishnu)

history.period: Believed ancient; traditionally said to predate the Venkateswara shrine
history.summary: The Sri Varahaswamy (Bhu Varahaswamy) Temple stands on the north-west corner of Swami Pushkarini, just north of the Sri Venkateswara Temple at Tirumala. According to local legend, Tirumala was originally Adi Varaha Kshetra: after rescuing the earth from the asura Hiranyaksha, Vishnu's boar avatar Varaha stayed on this hill, and when Venkateswara later came to reside here, he sought Varaha's permission. In gratitude, Venkateswara granted Varaha the right of first bell, first puja and first naivedyam (food offering), a privilege observed even today - all poojas are offered to Varaha Swamy before they are offered to Lord Balaji. Devotees are prescribed to have darshan of Varaha before Venkateswara, and a Tirumala pilgrimage is considered incomplete without it. The temple is administered by the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD) and the idol is the Adi Varaha form described in the Vaikhanasa Agama Sastras.

name: Sri Varahaswami Temple
town_description: Tirumala is a hill town at about 853 metres in the Seshachalam Hills, 22 km above Tirupati, centred on the Sri Venkateswara Temple - one of the most visited Vaishnavite pilgrimage centres in the world, drawing tens of millions of devotees annually. The town is spread over the seven peaks representing the seven heads of Adisesha and is administered almost entirely by the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD), which runs the temples, guest houses, free meal halls (annadanam), transport and tonsuring facilities.

travel.airport: Tirupati International Airport, Renigunta (approx. 40 km from Tirumala; taxis and app cabs available).
travel.railway: Tirupati Railway Station (approx. 22-23 km); well connected across India. Buses and cabs run regularly up the hill road.
travel.road: The temple is on the north-west corner of Swami Pushkarini, about 1 km from the Tirumala bus station and a short walk from the main Venkateswara Temple. Tirumala is reached from Tirupati by road (approx. 22 km ghat road) or the 3,550-step footpath; TTD runs free buses within the hill town.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March, when the weather on the hills is pleasant. Varaha Jayanti and Vaikuntha Ekadashi are the special festival days here; mornings before the Venkateswara darshan crowds peak are best for a quick, peaceful darshan of Varaha Swamy.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Generally 5:00 AM to 9:00 PM daily (verify - one listing notes Friday opening at 6:30 AM; a devotee account says 6:00 AM to 8:00 PM). No entry fee; traditional dress code applies; footwear not allowed inside.
